newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China may row back plan to dilute HK rights - Patten.
newsitem.headline: China may row back plan to dilute HK rights - Patten.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Monday that Beijing might consider "rowing back" its plan to dilute civil liberties and rights in the British colony, which China will take back on July 1.
In an interview with CNN, the governor also said a public consultation which the territory's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has promised to hold may prompt a change in Beijing's plan.

"If it is a genuine consultation, then we will find Mr Tung and the Chinese officials rowing back from the position that they've so far taken, because we know what people in Hong Kong think about these matters," Patten said.
"I think the extent to which the whole community has spoken out on civil liberties issues must have had some effect on Peking," Patten said in the interview monitored from Hong Kong.
"After all, they must want to win hearts and minds and not simply take over the real estate," he said.
China's parliament in February approved plans to strike out or amend a string of Hong Kong laws protecting civil liberties and rights, raising an uproar from the territory's pro-democracy camp.
